To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

retina transplanted into the brains of neonatal rats develops layers characteristic of normal retinal organization, that the transplanted retinae project to the host optic tract and visual nuclei, and that the host retina has an effect on the transplant projection.

(1) Retinae transplanted to the superior coliculus of newborn rats develop into organized retinal tissue; (2) Transplanted retinae project to retinorecipients structures; (3) The transplant projections are influenced by host retinal projections; (4) Transplanted retinal axons may be influenced by factors other than the target neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the formation of specific neuronal connections in the developing central nervous system.
the development of specific retinal projections to the superior coliculus and lateral geniculate nuclei.
the development of specific retinal projections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

1) the retinae transplanted to the brain of newborn rats develop into a structure resembling the normal retina; 2) this retina is able to project to the normal visual structures; 3) the distribution of the projections of the retina transplanted into one-eyed hosts is similar to that found in two-eyed hosts.
the transplanted retinae develop in an orderly manner within the host and that they are able to establish specific connections with host visual centers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the retina is a good transplant for the brain and the brain is a good transplant bed for the retina.
the retinae transplanted to the brain of rats develop into a functional retinal unit.

the retinae were capable of differentiating in the appropriate environment, that the retinae developed specific connections, that the transplant projection was influenced by the host retinal projection and by the host visual structures, and that the transplant projections were not influenced by the host visual input.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to transplant retinae to rat brains and demonstrate that they project to normal retinal targets.
the retina is a very useful model system for studying the mechanisms that underlie the development of neuronal connections.
the retinae are able to develop a normal organization in an ectopic environment, and are able to make connections with the host visual nuclei.
